title: Nitai of Tekoa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Mishnah Challah, chapter 4, mishnah 10: he brought portions of challah from Beitar, but they were not accepted. Hyman reports that the Jerusalem Talmud explains that, precisely because he was an eminent man, they refused them so others would not learn from his example to treat the practice as obligatory.

notes.text: Challah here means the dough-offering portions, not necessarily baked loaves. The prominent man’s example could be mistaken for an obligation.

The Mishnah names Nitai as the person who brought the portions. The consulted Yerushalmi discusses their disposal and spells the place Beitur. The reason concerning Nitai’s standing is reported as Hyman gives it.
